title: Terminator-trap invocation diary
content:
Summary:

Short running log of a recurring parsing failure when client code receives function-call style payloads. Failure symptom: some invocations return seemingly valid JSON for the tool call but the downstream parser throws a JSON parse error ("Unexpected token " at position X"). Hypothesis is that a "terminator" character (unescaped "\0" or stray control) or fragmented chunk boundary (stream splice) is being injected by the runtime's streaming/kvcache layer in a tiny fraction of requests.

Why this matters:
- Breaks structured output validation (evaluations flake)
- Causes downstream tool invocation errors (retries/timeouts)
- Hard to reproduce locally; only shows up in production traffic with specific prefix patterns

Repro / quick checklist tried so far:
- Replayed failing request payloads from traces via curl and python requests -> parsed fine locally (no error)
- Replayed using streaming API (chunked Transfer-Encoding) simulation -> sometimes reproduces error if speed throttled to ~5–10ms chunk intervals
- Forced kv-cache hit vs miss by toggling the prefix -> failure correlated with KV cache hit in 7/9 observed traces
- Added logging on receive path (raw bytes) in dev cluster -> found a 0x00 byte in 2/9 failing traces, not present in successful ones

Representative commands + outputs (copy-paste):

1) curl replay (non-streaming) that parsed fine:

curl -X POST https://api.redwood.dev/v1/invoke \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TEST" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '@payload.json'

-> 200 OK. body parsed by client: {"name":"my_tool","arguments":{"query":"status"}}

2) streaming simulation (python) that sometimes fails:

# python pseudo
import requests, time
with requests.post(url, stream=True, data=chunks_generator()) as r:
    for chunk in r.iter_content(chunk_size=None):
        print(repr(chunk))
        time.sleep(0.01)

Observed chunk containing a trailing '\\x00' at end of JSON string in failing runs: 
b'...}\\x00'

3) Raw log snippet from service raw-bytes capture (hex):
0000: 7b 22 6e 61 6d 65 22 3a 22 6d 79 5f 74 6f 6f 6c 22 2c 22 61 72 67 75 6d 65 6e 74 73 22 3a 7b 22 71 75 65 72 79 22 3a 22 73 74 61 74 75 73 22 7d 7d 00
                                                           ^-- trailing 00 in failing trace

Observed error from client JSON parser (node runtime):
SyntaxError: Unexpected token \u0000 in JSON at position 120
    at JSON.parse (<anonymous>)
    at parseFunctionCall (/app/lib/parse.js:42:18)

Notes about where the 0x00 might originate (current hypotheses):
- Hypothesis A: kvcache serialization path is appending a NULL byte as a delim for some pre-1.2 cached entries and streaming path doesn't strip it. Newer cache entries not affected.
- Hypothesis B: Kernel-level network stack or reverse-proxy is framing trailing zeros when content-length is computed vs actual bytes for chunked responses under certain buffer thresholds.
- Hypothesis C: Our streaming multiplexer (go) accidentally writes a zero byte when flushing an empty tail buffer for messages that exactly align with page boundaries.

Commands / experiments to isolate source (history):
- Added binary-safe read on receive and hex-dump to logging (PR attached in linked_artifacts). Result: confirmed 0x00 present before any client-side processing for failing traces.
- Re-ran with bypassing reverse-proxy (direct to runtime) -> still saw zeros. Lowers probability of Hypothesis B.
- Toggled kvcache TTL to force cache miss -> failure rate dropped from ~12% to ~1%. Suggests strong correlation with cached responses.
- Deployed temporary patch (runtime) that trims trailing 0x00 bytes before writing to stream -> failures disappeared in canary group for 48h. This is strong but crude mitigation.

Important edge-case observations:
- Trailing 0x00 only appears when the cached value size is a multiple of 4096 bytes in our tests (page boundary suspicion).
- Non-ASCII queries show same behavior (so not an encoding-only bug).
- Some clients (python requests) silently ignore 0x00 and parse OK; node JSON.parse throws. Explains inconsistent appearance across customers.

Hypotheses prioritized (next steps):
1) Root cause likely in the runtime serialization or our kvcache storage layer writing an extra null byte as a separator for page-aligned entries. This matches: cache correlation, 4096 pattern, and mitigates when we trim.
2) Secondary possibility: a compatibility shim added for older persisted cache blobs that requires a sentinel byte; new code path doesn't strip it on read-stream path.
3) Low chance: OS-level artifact. Already reduced by bypassing proxy.

Planned follow-ups (actionable):
- Patch: make kvcache write/read explicitly binary-safe and avoid sentinel bytes in persisted blob format (owner: Jordan). Target: small PR, include unit test that writes multiple sizes including multiples of page size.
- Add long-term fix for stream writer to never write trailing zeros (defensive). (owner: Priya).
- Add migration script to strip sentinel for existing persisted cache blobs and bump cache blob format version. (owner: Alex).
- Add more visibility: a metric exposing fraction of responses that contain control bytes on the wire; alert if >0.1% (owner: Observability).

Quick TODO (short):
- [ ] Add unit test to runtime to assert no 0x00 appended for aligned sizes
- [ ] Roll canary with trimming disabled after kvcache patch applied
- [ ] Draft runbook snippet: "If JSON parse errors with \u0000" -> check kvcache format version -> run strip migration -> route to devx oncall

Loose notes / ideas to remember:
- There might be legitimate uses of 0x00 inside tool arguments (rare) but current JSON string handling will always break. We should consider percent-encoding binary content inside arguments or use base64 wrapper for any binary payloads.
- Check other persistent stores (s3, local disk) for the same sentinel in older snapshots.

References / breadcrumbs to reproduce later:
- Trace ids with confirmed zeros: trace-redwood-20260201-0a3f, trace-redwood-20260210-9d2b
- Canary cluster where trimming patch ran: canary-nyc-3
- Quick repro: replay chunked stream with sleep 0.01 and force kvcache hit using test key `inv-terminator-test`.

End notes: this doc is messy — capturing scraps so we don't lose context. Will formalize into a short incident writeup when kvcache PR lands.

-- Alex
